why: IRAS's example: furniture bought for 3,000 with a tax written down value of 1,000 and sold for 200: proceeds lower than the TWDV, a balancing allowance of 800
IRAS's example: a computer bought for 2,000, written off, sold for 200: proceeds above the TWDV of nothing, a balancing charge of 200 (within the 2,000 allowed before)

IRAS's example: a van bought for 20,000 with a TWDV of 13,333.33 (IRAS rounds to 13,333) sold for 21,000: proceeds exceed the TWDV by 7,666.67 but the charge is restricted to the 6,666.67 allowed before (IRAS: 6,667)
sold for exactly the tax written down value: neither an allowance nor a charge
sold in the year it was bought for more than it cost: nothing was allowed before, so the charge, restricted to the allowances allowed before, is nothing
